stories.title: Tech Stocks Stumble as AI Spending Jitters Dent Wall Street
stories.whats_going_on: The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.5% as a fresh wave of selling hit major technology companies. Investors are increasingly questioning the massive spending on artificial intelligence and whether those heavy outlays will actually pay off.
stories.what_it_means: Markets have been flying high on tech optimism for months, but rising doubts about AI profitability are finally cooling down the enthusiasm. This volatility has spilled over into other sectors as traders re-evaluate risk.
stories.why_care: If you hold broad market index funds or tech pensions, expect a bit of turbulence in your statements while the market catches its breath.

stories.title: Oil Prices Surge Past $110 a Barrel on Supply Fears
stories.whats_going_on: Brent crude climbed above $110 a barrel for the first time since May. Traders ramped up bullish bets heading into the weekend as prospects for imminent supply relief dwindled.
stories.what_it_means: Geopolitical tensions and tightening supplies are pushing energy costs upward just as central banks try to keep inflation under control. Higher fuel costs quickly ripple through the wider economy.
stories.why_care: When global oil prices jump, everyday expenses like filling up the car and heating your home usually follow suit.

stories.title: US Mortgage Rates Hover Near 7.4% as Housing Slump Deepens
stories.whats_going_on: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage in the US held above 7 percent, remaining near 7.4%. Stubbornly high borrowing costs continue to compound affordability challenges for would-be buyers.
stories.what_it_means: Even as central banks weigh their next moves on interest rates, housing markets remain frozen by expensive borrowing terms. Buyers are finding themselves priced out as home prices stay stubbornly elevated.
stories.why_care: High mortgage rates make buying a home significantly more expensive, keeping many renters renting for longer.

stories.title: Banks Block AI Chatbots From Accessing Customer Accounts
stories.whats_going_on: Citi became the latest major US bank to restrict AI agents from directly accessing customer accounts. Lenders are increasingly worried that automated chatbots could automatically shift billions in deposits into higher-yielding accounts.
stories.what_it_means: Financial institutions are putting up digital guardrails as automated tools become sophisticated enough to manage personal money. Banks want to protect their stable deposits from sudden, algorithmic flights.
stories.why_care: It’s a reminder that while automated finance tools are handy, banks are tightening security to stop rogue software from moving your cash around.
